1.why: act - only D performs the 'evidence for a convention rather than for the thing depicted' reframe a main-idea stem about disputed depictions wants; B runs the opposite direction and C is a premise, not a thesis.

2.why: shape - A and D share the 'out of proportion to' frame while C is a null result and B a bare total, so the key is almost certainly in the A/D pair; nothing in the options says which taxon the passage is about.

3.why: knowledge - burrow aeration of waterlogged soil is the standard mechanism for crab-burrow facilitation of marsh plants; salt deposition (C) runs the wrong way and light at a soil opening (D) is not a real mechanism.

4.why: shape - two options independently put variety 1 at 12 at Site A, so C (40 there, with B's values transposed) is self-eliminating; A shows the full reversal a two-variety comparison wants, D only a near-tie.

5.why: none - three options corroborate 6 points at 10 minutes, killing D, and C stops at 1 week instead of the endpoint; A and B differ only in the 1-month number (34 vs 30) and the table alone decides that.

6.why: shape - 86 is Layer 4's total in B and Layer 1's in D, so B and D cannot both be read off the same table and both fall; between A and C only the numerator is in dispute, and 150/240 is the implausible one.

7.why: knowledge - clonal resprouting from the same individuals is the standard reading of a thicket that persists under heavy grazing; C and D both require seedling establishment, which is what grazing prevents.

8.why: act - only A ties the two villages together at the household level; B gives mere priority, C is irrelevant, and D (present everywhere from the first decade) actually undercuts a spread-by-contact argument.

9.why: act - B and C are a clean dichotomy (cold acting directly vs competition for the sugar) and the options-only tell is that C is the conclusion-shaped one; which limb the text supports is not recoverable here.

10.why: act - A is the only option that makes the divergence deliberate and known; B, C and D each blame an accident (haste, oversight, untranslatable verb), which is the distractor family.

11.why: none - A and B contradict each other on the same species pair (about as far vs three times as far), and three of four options assert retention time does not predict distance, so only the table separates them.

12.why: direction - the proposal names a distant northwestern source, and D is the only finding running that direction with a gradient (older the farther upriver); B and C argue against a distant source, A is about timber, not tin.

13.why: act - C reinterprets what the proxy has been measuring all along, which is what a post-dam divergence between rings and gauge licenses; D is the give-up option and B contradicts a dam that redistributes rather than removes water.

14.why: act - B is the split claim (material from far, working at the site) that main-idea keys take when sourcing and manufacture are both in evidence; A inverts it and C collapses it.

15.why: act - only C removes the proposed cue and reports the failure; A removes the destination, B is a truism about distance, D shows trail-following of the wrong trail.

16.why: shape - A and D agree that 28 percent remained at 20 m from 0.1 m, so that value is safe and the disputed 5 m pair (B 71/96 vs C 64/88) falls; D contrasts the extreme heights, A an intermediate one.

17.why: act - A is the only quotation that states the limit of the record itself rather than reporting an observation; D illustrates the same limit concretely and is the live alternative.

18.why: act - D is the 'less X than Y' correction of an expected account of revision, the shape main-idea keys take; C asserts the ordinary view and B is a different axis entirely.

19.why: knowledge - learned avoidance is the canonical brake on deceptive (non-rewarding) pollination; D reverses it, C denies the deception does any work, A invents a pollen cost.

20.why: act - only D reproduces the brittleness experimentally from the proposed process; A proposes a rival compositional cause and B and C are background conditions that discriminate nothing.

21.why: shape - A and C both put 31 species at 400 m, so B's 44 there is dead; C is also the mid-elevation peak that a species-richness-by-elevation figure almost always shows, while A asserts a flat pair and D a monotonic rise.

22.why: act - D is the only option with two directions in it (one species favored, two displaced); A, B and C are each a single uniform effect, which is the shape a contrast-reporting main idea rejects.

23.why: act - C is the only manipulation linking prior experience of the model plant to visits to the mimic; B shows the attraction is independent of the orchid, D is a quantitative aside, A is correlational co-occurrence.

24.why: act - the stem asks for the SECOND of two accounts, which in this frame is the lagging-indicator reading (ensembles registering a change pianists had already made); A is its mirror and C and D are the first account's 'moment of change' reading.

cross_item_rule: Two rules fired repeatedly. (1) PROSE ITEMS - the key is the option that holds two things in one relation (a reframe, a contrast, a 'less X than Y', a 'from this source, worked here'), while the distractors are each one flat cause. This picked items 1, 8, 10, 13, 14, 18, 20, 22, 23, 24 - ten of the eighteen non-figure items - without any passage. (2) FIGURE ITEMS - numeric corroboration across options: a value asserted by two or more options is a real table value, and any option contradicting it is dead. This fired on 4 (variety 1 = 12 at Site A, killing C), 6 (86 is Layer 4's total in B and Layer 1's in D, killing both), 16 (28 percent at 20 m corroborated, killing the 5 m pair B/C) and 21 (31 species at 400 m corroborated, killing B). It never left one option standing, but it halved four of the six figure items before the figure was consulted. Verdict on the author's claim: the rebuild succeeded on DIRECTION - no figure item was decidable by direction alone, and item 5 is genuinely clean (all four options assert the same growing advantage and only the number decides). It leaked in a different channel the rebuild did not watch: options that quote MUTUALLY INCONSISTENT values for the same cell, which is decidable with the figure covered. Item 21 is the weakest, because the corroborated 31-at-400 plus the canonical mid-elevation hump leaves one option.

constraining_pairs.note: Within item 4: A and D both put variety 1 at 12 galls at Site A; C puts it at 40 and hands B's 38/15 to the wrong variety. C is false without seeing the figure.

Within item 5: A and B state the same quantity - the twice-studied group's advantage at 1 month - as 34 and 30 points. One is false. D's 44 at 1 month makes a third incompatible value, and three options agree on 6 points at 10 minutes.

Within item 6: a scored total of 86 is Layer 4 in B and Layer 1 in D, while B calls Layer 1's total 96. The same table cannot support both, so B and D cannot both be legal. A and C agree on 240 (Layer 2) and 24/212 (Layer 3) and differ only in the Layer 2 numerator, 47 vs 150.

Within item 16: A and D agree that 28 percent of the 0.1 m playback remained at 20 m, corroborating that cell; B and C then give the same 5 m comparison as 71/96 and 64/88, so at most one of them is real.
Within item 21: A and C both read 31 species at 400 m, so B's 44 at 400 m is false. A and C then disagree about 800 m (31 vs 44), which is the only cell the figure is still needed for.

Within item 11: A and B describe the same species against the barbet with the same 23-minute retention gap but opposite distances - 'about as far' vs 'more than three times as far'. One is false; the other three options all assert the inverse relation, so B is the odd direction.
Within item 9: B (the cold acts directly) and C (competition, not the cold) are exhaustive and exclusive, so exactly one is true - but nothing in the option set says which.

Within item 24: A (ensembles resisting a change pianists had begun) and B (ensembles registering a change pianists had made) are the same fact with opposite valence; D asserts the pianists' change dates to the recordings themselves, contradicting both.

Across the figure items as a class: every one that leaked did so through this channel and not through direction. The distractors were built by perturbing individual cells of a real table, and the perturbations collide with the untouched cells quoted by sibling options.
